reasons: Only four of eight sections were available to review.
The row builder does not guard against empty entries.

terms.meaning: A check that a value is reasonable compared with a reference.
A number showing how sure the research agent is about a finding. It is optional.
A typical range taken from market data.
The part of the backend that searches for current market information.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for research screen
sections.what: Brings in the animation library, the store, icons for warnings, links and trends, and the research data types.
sections.why: Lists what the research screen needs.

sections.name: COMPONENT_LABELS
sections.title: Friendly component names
sections.what: Maps internal component codes such as modules and ess to readable names such as Modules and Energy Storage.
sections.why: Likely reason: the research data uses short codes, and users should see plain names.
sections.watch_out: A component code missing from this list has no friendly name here.

sections.name: CheckRow
sections.title: Validation row shape
sections.what: Describes one validation line: the field it checks, its status, an optional confidence number, and a detail sentence.
sections.why: Gives every check the same shape so they can be shown in one table.
sections.watch_out: Confidence is optional, so anything that displays it must handle it being missing.

sections.name: toRows
sections.title: Turning validation data into rows
sections.what: Turns the validation data into a list of rows. For each field it takes the user's value, or the calculated value if there is none, compares it with the market range or benchmark, and writes a sentence. If either side is missing, the sentence is left blank.
sections.why: Likely reason: a plain sentence lets non-experts read the comparison without interpreting the numbers.
sections.watch_out: An empty entry in the validation data would fail when read, because the builder reads its fields without checking first.

sections.name: WebResearchPanel (part 1)
sections.title: Choosing which research to show
sections.what: Shows the web research panel with a header and a row of buttons, one per component that has research. The first component is chosen by default, and clicking a button switches to that component. If there is no research at all, the panel shows nothing.
sections.why: Likely reason: the panel hides itself when there is nothing to show, so an empty page section does not appear.
sections.watch_out: Because the panel returns nothing when the research list is empty, a failed research step makes the whole section disappear without a message.

sections.name: WebResearchPanel (part 2)
sections.title: Summary headline for a component
sections.what: Shows the headline for the selected component: a green check if every range check passes, or an orange warning if any fail. A sentence gives the count of checks outside market range, along with a confidence percentage and the number of sources.
sections.why: Likely reason: the summary lets the user judge a component at a glance before reading the details.
sections.watch_out: Anything whose status is not exactly 'valid' counts as a problem, so a new status value would be flagged as a failure.

sections.name: WebResearchPanel (part 3)
sections.title: Range checks, suggestions, and sources list
sections.what: Lists each range check with its field name, detail text, and a status tag that is green for valid and red for anything else. Below that it shows the evidence source cards with a count, and a list of suggestions, each with its type and impact.
sections.why: Likely reason: the full list lets the user see each check and where the evidence comes from, not just a pass or fail.
sections.watch_out: Source cards use the link address as their unique key, so two sources with the same link would confuse the list.

sections.name: EvidenceCard
sections.title: Expandable evidence source card
sections.what: Shows one expandable card per source, with a numbered badge, the source title, and a relevance percentage. The first source opens by default. Opening a card shows the excerpt and a 'View source' link that opens the original page in a new tab.
sections.why: Likely reason: sources can be long, so they start collapsed to keep the page short, and the first one is open to show what a source looks like.
sections.watch_out: The panel trusts each link exactly as given, so a bad address only shows up when the user clicks it.

summary: The market research view: shows what the web research agent found about current prices and checks each input and output against market ranges.
purpose: Lets the user see whether their assumptions match market evidence, with sources.
why: Likely reason: users need to judge model assumptions against outside data before trusting the results.
how: Turns the validation results into simple rows. Each row has a status and, where both a value and a market range exist, a sentence comparing them. Component codes are shown with friendly names. The evidence cards and sources are drawn by parts of the file not reviewed here.
inputs: Research results from the store, including validation data for inputs and outputs.
outputs: Research tables, evidence cards, and source links on screen.
risks: Only four of eight sections were available to review. The row builder reads each validation entry without checking it exists first, so an empty entry would crash the screen.
debug: If a comparison sentence is blank, check that both a user or calculated value and a market range exist for that field. If the screen crashes, check the validation data for empty entries.
